description:
Venue model with GA capacities and full reserved seating: in-house authoring of sections/rows/seats, map versioning safe against sold inventory.

**Conditions of Success:**
- Staff can author and edit a seat map in the back office UI
- Maps are versioned; edits never orphan or duplicate sold/held seats
- GA and seated configurations coexist per venue

Lineage: docs/product/brief.md · docs/product/prd-v1.md (capability map).

comments.body: COS defined at epic level. Not yet decomposed — US-stories are created when the owner prioritizes this epic (Gate 1), per PRD 'Capability map'.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### ✅ Implementation readiness — CONCERNS

Epic TKT-3 decomposed into **5 vertical-slice stories** (TKT-101…TKT-105), Gate 1 pending.
Grounded in `docs/product/prd-v1.md` §Capability map (TKT-3) and a code-seam survey: the codebase
is **GA-only today** — no seated/section/row/seat structure, and **no back-office app** (storefront +
scanner only). So this epic is greenfield on a GA foundation with clear extension seams.

**Decomposition (ordered by dependency):**
| ID | Slice | Depends on | Class |
|---|---|---|---|
| TKT-101 | Back-office app shell — staff see the venue list (scaffold prefactor) | — | complex |
| TKT-102 | Author a draft seat map — sections/rows/seats | TKT-101 | complex |
| TKT-103 | Publish a seat map; a seated slot coexists with GA; event contract | TKT-102 | complex |
| TKT-104 | Edit a published map safely — pinned seats never orphaned/duplicated | TKT-103 | complex |
| TKT-105 | Back-office edit UI + version history + GA/seated toggle | TKT-103, TKT-104 | complex |

**COS coverage:**
- *Staff author & edit a seat map in the back-office UI* → TKT-101 (shell) + TKT-102 (author) + TKT-105 (edit/history).
- *Maps versioned; edits never orphan/duplicate sold/held seats* → TKT-102 (versioning from birth) + TKT-104 (safety invariant + pinning contract).
- *GA & seated coexist per venue* → TKT-103 (coexistence + publish contract), reinforced in TKT-105.

**Two scope decisions taken with the owner (2026-07-20):**
1. **Versioning proof is catalog-side.** TKT-104 proves the COS via a *seat-identity pinning contract*
   (a published seat identity is immutable across versions), NOT by building inventory seat-holds.
   The **held-seat** interplay is proven in **TKT-80** (US-017, TKT-4 epic), which already lists that
   AC and is hard-blocked on this epic. TKT-104's deliverable is the contract TKT-80 consumes.
2. **Back-office app scaffolded in-epic.** No admin surface exists; TKT-101 stands up `web/backoffice`
   + a gateway `/admin` route as a de-risked prefactor slice before any seat-map UI.

| Criterion | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Quality gates extracted | ✅ | `make check`, ADR-009 contract, ADR-004 TTL, ADR-022/020 migrations, ADR-002 tenancy — on every child |
| Vertical slices, one reviewable PR each | ⚠️ | TKT-104 (safety invariant + pinning-contract ADR + concurrency test) is the fattest; watch the ~400-line budget — split the ADR/contract from the invariant test if it grows |
| Prefactor split out first | ✅ | TKT-101 scaffolds the new app + gateway route before any domain logic |
| Ordered by dependency, no forward deps | ✅ | 101→102→103→104→105 (+103→105); cycle check passed |
| AC verifiable everywhere | ✅ | each AC is a concrete, testable assertion (rejections pinned, concurrency test, screenshots for UI) |
| Children linked + cycle check | ✅ | `blocks` edges wired dependency-correct; no cycle |
| Context-mémo baked per child | ✅ | ADR-004/005/014/017/018/026 resolved by area; binding rules verbatim |
| No unvalidated assumption a child silently depends on | ⚠️ | TKT-103 assumes inventory can *safely ignore* the seated event fork until TKT-80 — the plan must prove dispatch-on-schema tolerance (ADR-014 warns inventory hard-switches on schema) |

**Concerns (eyes-open, none blocking):**
1. **TKT-103 event-fork tolerance (TKT-103).** The seated `performance.published` fork must not break
   inventory's schema-switching consumer before TKT-80 exists. Named as an AC + a required test; the
   planning drafter is briefed via the mémo (ADR-014/ADR-017). Low residual risk, but real.
2. **TKT-104 sizing (TKT-104).** Backend safety invariant + a pinning-contract ADR + a concurrency
   test in one slice. Reviewable, but at the edge — acceptable; split the ADR out first if the plan
   estimates >400 lines.
3. **Held-seat COS lives across the epic boundary (TKT-104 → TKT-80).** Deliberate (owner decision),
   but it means TKT-3's versioning COS is only *fully* demonstrated once TKT-80 lands. TKT-104 proves
   the sold case and the contract; the held case is TKT-80's AC. Flagged so PO Review of TKT-104 does
   not expect the held-seat demo.

**Verdict:** CONCERNS — structurally sound, ordered, all COS covered by verifiable slices; the three
concerns are named risks the owner can weigh at Gate 1, not defects. **Ready to prioritize** (Gate 1):
the natural head is **TKT-101** (unblocks the whole chain).

_Classification: all five are **complex** (new domain model, cross-service event contract, concurrency
safety, and a net-new frontend app) — none carries `risk:low`; each gets the full plan gate._
